in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κωνσταντίνη είναι ελληνικής προέλευσης και σημαίνει 'απὸ τοῦ γένους' ή 'θύραθεν'. In Christian tradition, the name Konstance is associated with the virtue of constancy, or unshakeable faith. It is a feminine given name, symbolizing strength and perseverance in the face of adversity. In modern times, the name Konstance is often given to girls born into families with strong Christian values.

data.cultural_impact: In medieval Europe, the name Konstance (also known as Constance) was popular among Christian families due to the religious connotations of 'constancy' and 'faithfulness'. Many famous women with this name were revered for their unwavering belief and commitment to their religion and values. One notable example is Saint Konstance of Germany, who refused to marry an unfaithful suitor and was subsequently martyred for her steadfastness. Her story spread throughout Europe, inspiring many to name their children after this noble and faithful saint.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spiritual thought, the name Konstance carries the deep meaning of unwavering faith and rock-solid devotion. It serves as a reminder of the importance of remaining steadfast in one's beliefs, even in the face of adversity. Konstance is a name that inspires strength and resilience, indicating the deep inner reserves of religious faith that can sustain one through life's challenges. The name also speaks to the transformative power of faith, as demonstrated in the story of Saint Konstance, who remained steadfast in her convictions to the very end.
